messages.subject: sampling effort and polygons
parts:
Can effort as non-binary values be used with polygons? The secr-varyingeffort.pdf suggests you can, but the section 2.5 Miscellaneous suggests this is not necessary so not sure if non-binary effort is implemented for detector=polygon

I have tried the following statement

trappoly <- read.traps(file = 'CUISpoly500.txt', detector = 'polygon', binary.usage = FALSE)

where the usage value is normalized and below is the first polygon of the text data file

# polygon easting northing usage
1   456285.47058 3397700.5272 -0.383
1   456785.47058 3397700.5272 -0.383
1   456785.47058 3398200.5272 -0.383
1   456285.47058 3398200.5272 -0.383
1   456285.47058 3397700.5272 -0.383


When I try to use read.traps I get the following error message:

Error in dimnames(usge) <- list(tempID, 1:nocc) : 
  'dimnames' applied to non-array

If I truncate the usage data from the text file and simply read in polygons I can analyze the data, but of course this assumes sampling effort is constant across polygons.

If it is not possible to use non-binary data with polygon sampling, perhaps there is another approach I can use to model the data?  Scats were collected by walking roads, trails, and linear habitats (interdune meadow) on an island. We recorded the UTM coordinate where the scat was collected but we did not record track logs of the path walked.  However, I can create an index to effort by summing the length of paths walked (just not the exact paths), which is why I thought a non-binary measure of effort might work.

Thanks,


Duane Diefenbach

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: sampling effort and polygons
parts:
Hi Duane

This is a simple bug. The code for usage with polygon detectors unintentionally collapsed a matrix to a vector when there was a single occasion. This happens by default when the result from '[' would otherwise be a 1-column matrix.

I read this yesterday in Patrick Burns' estimable 'R inferno' 8.1.44: "NOTE: Failing to use drop=FALSE inside functions is a major source of bugs", and so it is.

I'm actively developing a new version, and will get you a fixed pre-release copy if that helps.

Murray
